title: Explore architecture and module boundaries
summary: The current authoritative runtime is a layered desktop stack: React/Vite UI in `desktop/src`, a Tauri/Rust host in `desktop/src-tauri`, and a Node/TypeScript MCP gateway in `src-ts`. The repository still carries migration-era adapter seams and compatibility paths, but the default delivery path is no longer the historical Python/Web stack.

notable_absences.note: No top-level Python `src/` directory exists in this checkout, which matches the README claim that Python gateway sources may be absent in the Node-first baseline.

runtime_entry_points.note: Creates the React root and mounts `App` only.
Composes the four-pane shell and delegates startup/view-model logic to hooks.
Chains theme startup and backend bootstrap.
In Tauri only, syncs UI gateway override into Rust and invokes `start_backend`.
Resolves gateway base, asks Rust for runtime base in Tauri, and uses `call_api` via invoke or direct fetch in browser/dev mode.
Owns gateway process/base resolution, health checks, request proxying, and the explicit command contract consumed by React.
Builds the HTTP gateway, wires container-backed dependencies, and exposes health/config/chat/memory/graph/agent/critic/skills/workflow/writing/mcp-admin endpoint groups.

module_boundaries.boundary: React components stay mostly presentational while `useAppViewModel` collects state from stores and specialized hooks before mapping to shell props.
The desktop client does not own process management; it talks through `api/client.ts`, which switches between browser fetch and Rust-hosted proxy calls.
Rust maintains child process lifecycle, base override precedence, and cleanup semantics, making Tauri the formal contract surface between UI and gateway.
The TypeScript gateway is organized around MCP endpoint families and a service registry rather than a monolithic app controller.
Service resolution is centralized in an Inversify-based container that separates migrated services from adapter-backed or placeholder engine contracts.
Legacy web/Python surfaces are retained as compatibility entry points, but the repo now explicitly marks them non-authoritative.

recent_workflow_context.relevance: Shows the TypeScript migration was still hardening workflow/agent/search seams on 2026-04-04 and explicitly called out placeholder container/search behavior.
Confirms the data layer remained migration-sensitive on 2026-04-04, with null bridges and no-op integration adapters identified as risks.
Provides the latest authority signal that Node-first runtime and current-vs-historical documentation boundaries were explicitly hardened on 2026-04-07.

strengths: Runtime responsibility is cleanly split: React handles shell composition, Rust owns process/runtime coordination, and the TypeScript gateway owns HTTP/MCP endpoint orchestration.
The gateway has an explicit built-in service registry (`memory`, `graph`, `search`, `workflow`, `critic`, `agent`, `skills`) instead of scattering runtime routes across unrelated modules.
The repository now has a clearer authority map in README and governance handoffs, which reduces ambiguity about the current delivery path.

architectural_risks.title: Migration-era adapter seams remain part of the main backend assembly
architectural_risks.detail: The container still distinguishes migrated services from placeholder or adapter-backed contracts, and several integration adapters are intentionally no-op/stubbed depending on flags. This means the runtime is coherent, but not all boundaries are fully native or equally hardened.

architectural_risks.title: Dual-runtime compatibility still increases boundary complexity
architectural_risks.detail: Current authority is Node-first, but Rust still carries runtime selection logic for Node/Python sidecars and the launcher script still exposes `--runtime python`. The compatibility path is explicit, yet it keeps extra lifecycle and support complexity in the critical startup chain.

architectural_risks.title: Historical architecture docs lag the current checkout shape
architectural_risks.detail: The active README says `desktop + src-ts` is authoritative, but `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` still describes a Python `src/*` architecture that is not present in this checkout. This is a documentation-boundary risk more than a runtime risk, but it can mislead future changes.

key_findings: The repository has converged on a three-stage runtime: React desktop shell -> Tauri/Rust host -> Node/TypeScript gateway.
The UI shell is intentionally thin; orchestration is pushed into hooks and stores rather than embedded in top-level components.
Rust, not React, is the operational boundary for sidecar startup, health resolution, and request proxying.
The backend is centered on `src-ts/gateway-server.ts` and a built-in MCP service registry, not on a Python web server in this checkout.
TypeScript migration hardening is still visible through adapter-heavy container seams and no-op/stub integration adapters.
Authority documentation improved on 2026-04-07, but older architecture docs still describe a Python-first layout that no longer exists here.
